newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open weaker on strong U.S. GDP data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open weaker on strong U.S. GDP data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker in active trade on Wednesday, softening in tandem with weaker U.S. treasuries on the release of stronger than expected U.S. gross domestic product data, analysts said.

"The (U.S.) GDP came in way higher than expectations, way higher than the highest expectations, so naturally we're selling off," said Jim Webber, director of fixed-income research with TD Securities Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark fell C$0.33 to C$108.95 to yield 7.232 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond fell 12/32 to yield 7.02 percent.
The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 21 basis points from 23 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.

Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets weakened after the U.S. report, which showed that GDP grew at an annual rate of 5.6 percent in the first quarter. A Reuters survey of economists had expected, on average, a 4.1 percent rise in the first quarter.
In Canada, an economic report showed Canada's monthly GDP data rose 0.5 percent in February, in line with expectations. The Canadian report had little impact on markets.
The U.S. report dominated markets as it increased speculation that the U.S. Federal Reserve would hike interest rates in the near future.
On Tuesday, Canadian bonds posted their biggest one-day gains since the Quebec referendum of 1995, as weaker than expected U.S. economic data spurred hopes that U.S. rates would not rise.

"It's not like we're pricing in a whole bunch of Fed hikes again based on having been wrong yesterday. It's just that things maybe got a little bit too bullish yesterday and at least some of that is being given back," said TD's Webber.
Canada's 10-year benchmark bonds fell C$0.33 to C$101.95 to yield 6.719 percent. The U.S. bond fell 9/32 to yield 6.80 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds was eight basis points, unchanged from Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.18 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.27 percent.
